ArtifactDate: 5th century BC, rebuilt 2nd century BC (destroyed c. 110 BC)
Description: The Samaritan temple on Mount Gerizim, excavated by Yitzhak Magen: a sacred precinct with a temple, courtyards, and a city that housed its priests. It was the rival sanctuary to Jerusalem that the Samaritan woman meant when she told Jesus, 'Our fathers worshipped in this mountain.' John Hyrcanus destroyed it around 110 BC, but Samaritans still worship on the mountain today.
BiblicalSignificance: John 4 suddenly has a mountainside address. The woman's question was not abstract theology but a live wound between two peoples and two sanctuaries — and Jesus answered it by pointing past both mountains to worship in spirit and in truth.
Interpretations: Scholars broadly accept the excavated precinct as the Samaritan temple of John 4; the exact layout of its earliest phase is less certain than its existence and location.
